## DG4 round 3, domain-reviewer: **FAIL**

My three round-2 findings are fixed. But I found a new High, mandatory defect, plus two Medium ones, so this candidate cannot pass.

The candidate checks out: `sha256:890faa12…84b6` with 1459 files, the same in the repo and in a full disposable clone of `c94b2a2` (source `925f0bc`). Every candidate check passed:
- **Gate validators:** `--register DG4`, `--historical` for DG3, DG2 and DG1, and `--pipeline` all exit 0.
- **Build and unit tests:** typecheck, build, lint and unit pass on Node 22 and 24. Unit: 2819 passed, plus 259 passed with 2 skipped by design.
- **Integration:** 1960 of 1960.
- **Real-stack probes, EN and AR:** 49/49, 38/38 and 127/127.

### Round-2 findings (all CLOSED_VERIFIED)
- **F-DG4-122:** the value gap now shows as a percentage, never as money. Real numbers render as 100 %, 25 %, −20 % and 12.5 % on T10, the Executive Overview and the Finance dashboard, in English and Arabic.
- **F-DG4-123:** with my test data (revenue 300, margin 70, cash saving 20, avoided cost 45), the value headlines show 90, 300 and 45 on all four screens. Each is labelled with its basis, 435 appears nowhere, and each drill-down sums to its headline. If a transformation has only revenue uplift and avoided cost, the profit-and-cash headline and the Value status show "not applicable", never 0 or green.
  - **Rule judgement:** I accept the D-119 headline basis against the source (M0172, B0145). I reject only how the Value status is scoped; see F-DG4-126.
  - **KBE-R6's design choices:** I accept (a), (b), (c) and (e) and reject (d) (raised as F-DG4-127). I accept that the DG3 business-case totals keep their different basis.
- **F-DG4-124:** the DG4 stage history is now legal at every step, and the validators pass.

### New findings
| ID | Severity | Owner | What happens |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-DG4-125 | **High, mandatory** | frontend-ux-engineer | A 12 % KPI (stored as 0.12) shows as **"0.12 %"** on the dashboards, in English and Arabic. The F-DG4-122 fix sends `percentage` and `%` values to the new percent formatter without multiplying by 100. FE-R5's handback assumes these values are already percentages, which contradicts ADR-0028 §3. It affects every percentage KPI, including most adoption indicators. It is partly pre-existing: before the fix the same value showed "0.12 percentage". |
| F-DG4-126 | Medium | solution-architect | The Value status now ignores unvalidated revenue uplift and avoided cost. With 70 of margin fully validated and 300 of revenue uplift (or avoided cost) planned but unvalidated, the Value status is **Green** on T10, the Overview and the Finance rows. The source rule (B0095, M0248) bases it on the validated benefit gap. The repair caused this: the round-2 code would have shown this case Red, though I worked that out from the code rather than running it. It is partly my fault: my round-2 expected text put the gap on the profit-and-cash basis and said nothing about the other bases. This is my partial rejection under D-119, so its escalation clause applies to this part only. |
| F-DG4-127 | Medium | kpi-benefits-engineer | The Portfolio area still shows each initiative's value as one unlabelled sum of all five financial classes: **435** in my test data. This is the same mixing that F-DG4-123 removed from the headlines. |

### Disclosures
- **Probe failures by design:** these were my assertions of the source rule, and each failure is one of the findings above:
  - the format probe: 4 failures;
  - the percentage-KPI screen probe: 4 of 4;
  - my in-process probe: 2 tests (R3-6 and R3-8).
- **My interference with Node 24 typecheck:** its first run exited 2 because I deleted my probe file from the clone while it ran. A clean re-run passed.
- **My probe not loading:** integration run 1 exited 1 only because my own probe file couldn't load (a dependency it couldn't resolve from that folder). After I fixed the import, I re-ran it alone.
- **Percentage-KPI screen evidence:** the dev seed has no percentage KPI and the stack runs no recalculation worker. So that screen test feeds the real web app a captured API response with one added row, using the exact value object the real API produced in-process.
- **F-DG4-126 and F-DG4-127 have no screenshots.** Both are proven on the API only; I show the code path that puts those values on screen.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG4/round-3/`:
- domain-reviewer.json
- domain-reviewer.findings.json
- domain-reviewer.verifications.json

Evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG4/domain/round-3/`.
